answer: Agents gain voting weight only after locking a bond through a dawn-to-dawn challenge: each must complete a random task, and independent agents verify the result. Fabricated or copied work can trigger a slash of the bond. A relic of past success may build reputation, but cannot replace the fresh test. A sybil attacker must therefore lock capital for every identity and risk losing it, while producing distinct work; a plume of cheap accounts alone earns no influence.
